posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — The more Indian stocks I research, the more I think numbers are the least interesting part of the story. Those three figures could describe a great compounder or a business about to disappoint. What separates them is almost never in the screener. It’s the context: A one-off in “other income” that made profit look better than the business actually was Management tone on the concall. posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — The most annoying part for me is that the data and indicators are available, but understanding what the market is actually going to do is still difficult. Even when my analysis suggests a bearish move, the market can continue moving in the opposite direction. It’s hard to know whether the analysis is wrong or the market just needs more time to react.

posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — @MarketDeckIndia @TraderJini I’m Dishant, I built OptFolio (www.optfolio.in), so I’m biased. For the “profit up 30%, but why” question, I split the change into three parts from the P&L: revenue growth, operating margin change, and other income or one-offs. Then I check whether cash from operations moved with operating profit; if it didn’t, that’s usually the real story. posts.author: Kabir_B
posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — For me, one thing I really enjoy is just observing things around me. Sometimes what you see in your daily life can be a pretty good research tool, especially for consumer-facing businesses. Of course, you have to filter out the noise and not take one observation as a conclusion. The most annoying part for me is probably figuring out which information actually matters and which is just noise. There is so much data and commentary available that sometimes filtering it is harder than finding it.

posts.author: DishantSR
posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — My workflow is fairly boring, but it cut my tab count a lot. I start with 10 years of financials and the peer table on Screener, and judge ROCE against the company’s own history and its 3–4 closest peers rather than as an absolute number. 18% is strong for a capital-heavy business but fairly ordinary for an asset-light one. posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — I research Indian stocks regularly, and my process is held together by tabs and spreadsheets.
